This article walks through a first search: setting up credentials, finding
providers near a ZIP code, turning the results into a table, and starting from
a place instead of a ZIP code. Each step links to a longer article.

The code here needs a connection to the HIV.gov Locator API. If this copy of
the article was built without one, you see the code but not its output.

## What the package does

The HIV.gov Locator API lists places that offer HIV testing, prevention and
care, and related services such as hepatitis C testing, mental health care and
housing help. CDCLocator sends your questions to the API and returns the
answers as tibbles.

There are four functions you will use:

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cdc_providers()` | Finds providers within a radius of a ZIP code |
| `cdc_providers_tidy()` | Turns those results into one plain row per provider |
| `cdc_address_place()` | Finds the ZIP code for a city and state |
| `cdc_address_point()` | Finds the ZIP code for a latitude and longitude |

A fifth, `cdc_locator_set_credentials()`, sets your credentials for one
session.

## Step 1: credentials

The API needs a client ID and a client token. HIV.gov issues them on request;
see [HIV.gov's announcement of the Locator
API](https://www.hiv.gov/blog/announcing-the-locator-api).

The best place to keep them is your `.Renviron` file, which R reads when it
starts. Open it with `usethis::edit_r_environ()`, add these two lines with your
own values, save, and restart R:

```
CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN=your-client-token
```

Check that R can see them. This prints `TRUE TRUE` without showing the values:

```{r}
nzchar(Sys.getenv(c("CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID", "CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN")))
```

`vignette("credentials-and-networks")` covers other ways to supply them, how
to keep the token safe, and which networks the API accepts.

## Step 2: find providers near a ZIP code

```{r}
library(CDCLocator)

providers <- cdc_providers("20176", radius = 5)
providers
```

Three things to notice:

- **The ZIP code is a string.** `"02110"` keeps its leading zero; the number
  `02110` would become `2110`, so the package refuses numbers.
- **`radius` is in miles**, a whole number from 1 to 50. The default is 10.
- **With no `services` argument, every service is searched.** The API returns
  nothing when all 14 services are asked for at once, so the package asks for
  three at a time: five requests, half a second apart. The search takes a few
  seconds.

The result has one row per provider record and three columns: `type`, `id`,
and `attributes`, which holds the details in nested form.

## Step 3: one row per provider

`cdc_providers_tidy()` unpacks the details into ordinary columns:

```{r}
tidy <- cdc_providers_tidy(providers)
names(tidy)
tidy[, c("name", "street", "city", "zipcode", "contact_telephone", "distance")]
```

`distance` is in miles from the ZIP code you searched. `languages` is a list
column, because a provider can list several. `vignette("working-with-results")`
describes every column and shows how to sort, map and save the table.

## Step 4: choose services

To search for particular services, name them:

```{r}
testing <- cdc_providers(
  "20176",
  radius = 10,
  services = c("hivtesting", "stdtesting", "hepc")
)
```

A provider is returned if it offers **any** of the services you name. The 14
service names, and what each covers, are in
`vignette("services-and-searching")` and `?cdc_providers`. Case doesn't
matter: `"HIVtesting"` works too.

## Step 5: start from a place or a point

The provider search only takes a ZIP code. If you have a city and state, or a
latitude and longitude, look up the ZIP code first:

```{r}
peoria <- cdc_address_place("Peoria", "IL")
peoria

cdc_address_point(40.69365, -89.58899)
```

Each returns one row with the city, the full state name, the ZIP code and its
coordinates. Pass the ZIP code on:

```{r}
cdc_providers(peoria$zipcode, radius = 10, services = "hivtesting") |>
  cdc_providers_tidy()
```

## When something goes wrong

Errors say which function and argument they're about, and pass on what the
API said. The most common ones:

- **"CDC Locator API credentials not found"**: R can't see your credentials.
  Go back to step 1.
- **HTTP 403 Forbidden**: either the key was refused, or your network was. The
  API has refused requests from outside the US and from some cloud servers.
- **HTTP 500 with "No point found for address"**: the API doesn't know that
  ZIP code.

`vignette("troubleshooting")` lists every error with what to do about it.
